report.title: Checkout Latency Due to Inventory Client Connection Pool Reduction
report.summary: Checkout API p95 latency rose sharply after a recent release reduced the inventory client connection pool size. Slow traces indicate significant time spent waiting for database connections.

findings.text: Checkout API p95 latency increased from 420ms to 2840ms, and error rate rose to 6.8% from 14:15 UTC.
A checkout release at 14:12 UTC reduced the inventory client connection pool maximum from 20 to 5.
One representative slow trace shows db.pool.acquire waiting for 2190ms within inventory.reserve.
Database CPU and payment authorization times remained stable, while database pool pending requests increased to 84.

nextSteps: Confirm the exact connection pool configuration currently deployed in the checkout service's inventory client.
Validate if reverting the connection pool size to its previous value (20) resolves the latency and error rate.
Monitor checkout service metrics for improvement after the proposed change is applied.
report.uncertainty: While the temporal correlation and trace data strongly suggest the connection pool change as the cause, direct causality has not been definitively proven through experimentation (E3, E5).
report.customerUpdate: We are investigating an issue impacting the speed of our checkout process. Our teams are working to identify and resolve the problem, and we will provide another update as soon as more information is available. There is no confirmed impact on completed orders.

proposal.action: Revert the checkout service's inventory client connection pool maximum from 5 to 20.
proposal.rationale: The latency and error rate increase correlates with a release that reduced the inventory client connection pool. Slow traces indicate database connection pool contention.
proposal.expectedEffect: Reduced checkout API latency and error rates, with inventory.reserve and db.pool.acquire times returning to baseline.

report.title: Checkout Degradation Linked to Inventory-Database Network Path Policy Update
report.summary: Checkout API experienced elevated latency and errors starting 17:14 UTC. Evidence suggests a firewall policy update on the inventory-to-database path at 17:11 UTC led to increased connection rejections and slow TCP handshakes to the database, impacting inventory services.

findings.text: Checkout API p95 latency increased from 480ms to 3180ms and error rate rose to 7.4% from 0.4% at 17:14 UTC.
Slow traces show 2450ms for tcp.connect to inventory-db in the inventory service, observed in 16 of 20 slow samples.
Network flow records indicate 18% rejected connections to inventory-db from 17:14 UTC, up from 0.1% baseline.
A firewall policy update for the inventory-to-database path was applied at 17:11 UTC.

proposal.action: Revert the firewall policy update applied at 17:11 UTC on the inventory-to-database path.
proposal.rationale: Increased rejected connections (E3) and slow TCP connection handshakes to inventory-db (E2) started at 17:14 UTC, correlating with a firewall policy update on that path at 17:11 UTC (E5). This is a leading hypothesis for the checkout API degradation (E1).
